```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 96)
has_plots <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("viridisLite", quietly = TRUE)
```

Analysis returns data first: tables with stable identifiers, documented units
and explicit perspectives. Plots and reports are built from those tables, so
every figure can be checked against its numbers. No model or Python is needed;
model evaluations are optional and labelled when used.

## A position

`g3_analyse_position()` searches every legal action with a full window, so the
alternatives' scores are exact for the completed depth and directly
comparable. Scores are heuristic units from the side to act's point of view.

```{r}
st <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()$state
an <- gambitR3D::g3_analyse_position(st, budget = list(nodes = 60000L, depth = 2L))
an
```

## A game

```{r}
game <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()
for (i in 1:24) {
  if (gambitR3D::g3_is_terminal(game$state)) break
  agent <- if (game$state$side == "white") "search" else "greedy"
  d <- gambitR3D::g3_choose_action(game$state, agent, budget = list(nodes = 4000L))
  game <- gambitR3D::g3_game_apply(game, d$action_id)
}
res <- gambitR3D::g3_analyse_game(game, budget = list(nodes = 2000L))
res
```

Each table has a definition in the feature dictionary, with unit, denominator
and missing-value policy:

```{r}
dict <- gambitR3D::g3_feature_dictionary()
head(dict[dict$table == "positions", c("name", "unit", "denominator")])
```

Mobility counts actions and distinct destinations separately (a promotion or
a platform's two orientations inflate the first). Attack maps come from the
engine's threat semantics, not from legal moves. Tactical labels carry their
claim strength: exact (check, capture, mate, pins tested by removing the
piece), bounded search (a forced line within the budget) or heuristic (forks,
hanging pieces, consequential platform actions, each with its definition).

```{r}
head(res$moves[, c("ply", "actor", "action_type", "capture", "check")], 8)
table(res$tactics$label, res$tactics$claim_strength)
```

Move loss compares the played action with the best alternative under the same
evaluator and budget. It is stored raw, including negative values caused by
finite search; a clipped display column is labelled as such.

## Plots

```{r trajectory, eval = has_plots, fig.alt = "Expected-score trajectory of the game from White's side"}
gambitR3D::g3_plot_game(res, metric = "expected_score", perspective = "white")
```

The expected score here is a fixed logistic mapping of heuristic units,
labelled as uncalibrated: it is a readable scale, not a probability.

Heatmaps keep the seven boards apart: overlapping projected coordinates are
different squares.

```{r heatmap, eval = has_plots, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Occupancy heatmap per physical square, one panel per board"}
gambitR3D::g3_plot_board_heatmap(res, metric = "occupancy", coordinate_space = "board_local")
```

## Comparing agents

`g3_compare_agents()` plays paired games from the same starting positions with
the agents' colours swapped, under equal budgets. Games that hit the ply cap
are counted as truncated, never as draws, and the score is reported both for
completed games and as bounds over all scheduled games.

```{r}
cmp <- gambitR3D::g3_compare_agents(
  c(search = "search", random = "random"),
  budget = list(nodes = 1500L), seeds = 1L, pairs = 1L, max_plies = 40L
)
cmp$games[, c("white_agent", "black_agent", "status", "agent1_score")]
cmp$summary[, c("scheduled", "completed", "truncated", "completed_score",
                "scheduled_lower_bound", "scheduled_upper_bound")]
```

With one starting position this is descriptive. `vignette("experiments")`
explains the design for real comparisons.

## A collection

`g3_analyse_database()` takes a database, a database path, game files or a list
of games. It works in chunks, can be cancelled and resumed from its output
directory, and records failures per game.

```{r}
short <- gambitR3D::g3_game_event(
  gambitR3D::g3_game_apply(gambitR3D::g3_new_game(), "m:W:0:1-W:0:2"), "resign"
)
coll <- gambitR3D::g3_analyse_database(list(game, short), evaluator = "none")
coll
```

## Reports

```{r}
out <- gambitR3D::g3_export_analysis_report(res, file.path(tempdir(), "game-report.html"))
out$files[, c("file", "bytes")]
```

The HTML report is a single file with embedded figures, escaped game text, the
evaluator, budget, rules hash and score perspective. It opens without a network
connection.
